post.description: Internal-surface enqueue. Auth is the M1 signed assertion path (not site-admin-only). Assertion claims supply `callingOperationId` and `originalRequestId`. On a live `dedupe_key` collision the existing job is upserted (run_at pushed, request refreshed) and returned with 200; otherwise a new job is created with 201.

operation_id.description: Target OpenAPI operationId (must exist and carry the background tag).

request.description: Capped request payload for the target operation (serialized size ≤ 16 KB including this object's path_params/query/body).

run_at.description: Absolute earliest claim time. Ignored when delay_ms is also set if the implementation prefers delay_ms; typically use one or the other.

delay_ms.description: Relative delay in milliseconds from enqueue time before the job becomes claimable. Alternative to run_at.

dedupe_key.description: Optional key unique among non-terminal jobs. Re-enqueue with the same live key upserts and returns the existing job (200).

concurrency_key.description: Optional key limiting concurrency (at most one running job per key).

priority.description: Claim priority; higher values are claimed first. Defaults to 0.

on_behalf_of.description: Explicit authority override for enqueueOnBehalfOf. When present, both user_id and authority evidence are required; the job runs as that user under the given grant instead of deriving authority from the caller's request context.

user_id.description: Acting user for the enqueued job.

authority.description: Evidence grant for the override (request, importer, or cron kind).

200.description: Existing job returned after a dedupe-key upsert.

400.description: Request payload exceeds the 16 KB serialized size cap.

403.description: Forbidden - calling operation is not allowed to enqueue the target (trigger-map violation).

422.description: Unknown operationId, or the target operation is not tagged `background`.

429.description: Spawn cap exceeded for this originalRequestId chain.

request.description: Capped request payload delivered to the target operation (serialized size ≤ 16 KB). Path params, query, and body are optional and substituted into the operation's path template / request.

path_params.description: Path template substitutions keyed by parameter name.

query.description: Query string parameters keyed by name.

body.description: JSON request body for the target operation, when any.

authority.description: Root grant for the job chain (copied verbatim by children). Discriminated on `kind`. Wire form excludes the embedded enqueue assertion token.

oneOf.description: A user's authenticated request (or an admin action) instigated the chain. Evidence is the originating request id (also in the audit log).

user_id.description: User who made the originating request.

oneOf.description: A webhook arrived for a channel subscription; the importer's creator authorized scanning this channel. Evidence is the importer row.

user_id.description: Importer creator whose authority is used.

importer_id.description: Short id of the importer row that authorized the chain.

oneOf.description: A cron tick fired for an enabled job; the admin who last enabled it is the recorded authority. Evidence is the cron job name.

user_id.description: Admin who enabled the cron job (`enabled_by`).

cron_job_name.description: Name of the cron job that enqueued this chain.

job.description: Wire form of a queued API-call job; field names match the `job` row and nested JSON. Omits internal columns (`heartbeat_at`, `updated_at`). Authority is the discriminated evidence grant without the raw enqueue assertion token (detail endpoints may return that separately as `authority_assertion`).

id.description: Short identifier for the job (from generateShortId).

status.description: Lifecycle state. `pending`/`retrying` are claimable; `running` is in delivery; `succeeded`/`dead`/`cancelled` are terminal.

operation_id.description: Target OpenAPI operationId resolved at delivery time.

request.description: Capped request payload delivered to the target operation (serialized size ≤ 16 KB). Path params, query, and body are optional and substituted into the operation's path template / request.

path_params.description: Path template substitutions keyed by parameter name.

query.description: Query string parameters keyed by name.

body.description: JSON request body for the target operation, when any.

user_id.description: Acting user whose authority the job runs under.

authority.description: Root grant for the job chain (copied verbatim by children). Discriminated on `kind`. Wire form excludes the embedded enqueue assertion token.

oneOf.description: A user's authenticated request (or an admin action) instigated the chain. Evidence is the originating request id (also in the audit log).

user_id.description: User who made the originating request.

oneOf.description: A webhook arrived for a channel subscription; the importer's creator authorized scanning this channel. Evidence is the importer row.

user_id.description: Importer creator whose authority is used.

importer_id.description: Short id of the importer row that authorized the chain.

oneOf.description: A cron tick fired for an enabled job; the admin who last enabled it is the recorded authority. Evidence is the cron job name.

user_id.description: Admin who enabled the cron job (`enabled_by`).

cron_job_name.description: Name of the cron job that enqueued this chain.

original_request_id.description: Chain-root request id (user request / webhook X-Request-ID, or cron-tick id). Copied from parent on chained enqueues; joins audit_event.request_id.

enqueued_by_operation_id.description: Calling operationId that enqueued this job (trigger-map edge).

parent_job_id.description: Short id of the job that enqueued this one, or null at the chain root.

run_at.description: Earliest time the job may be claimed for delivery.

dedupe_key.description: Optional key unique among non-terminal jobs. Re-enqueue with the same live key upserts (pushes run_at, refreshes request) and returns the existing job.

concurrency_key.description: Optional key limiting concurrency: at most one running job per key (e.g. `matter:{id}`).

priority.description: Claim priority; higher values are claimed first. Default 0.

attempt.description: Number of delivery attempts consumed so far (0 before first claim).

max_attempts.description: Maximum delivery attempts before the job becomes dead (exhausted).

result.description: Outcome of the latest terminal or failed attempt. Null while the job has not yet finished an attempt that records a result. `error_body` is set only on failure and capped at 8 KB.

status_code.description: HTTP status code from the delivery attempt, when available.

error_body.description: Capped error response body recorded only on failure.

terminal_reason.description: Why the job became terminal. Null when the job succeeded or result is from a non-terminal retryable failure mid-flight.

created_at.description: When the job row was created.

started_at.description: When the current (or last) delivery attempt started; null if never claimed.

finished_at.description: When the job reached a terminal status; null while still active.

code.description: A short, machine-readable error code, for when HTTP status codes are not sufficient.

message.description: A human-readable description of the error.
message.example: The requested resource could not be found.
